content:
Hi all,

We are happy to annouce EconCSLib, the initial effort of a project to formalize Computational Economics (also known as EconCS) in Lean.

EconCS is an area at the intersection of economics, mathematics, and theoretical computer science. It studies topics such as game theory, mechanism design, auctions, markets, social choice and many others from a mathematical and algorithmic perspective.

Our motivation is simple: while there have been previous efforts formalizing specific topics and results in EconCS, there has not yet been a systematic effort to build a comprehensive library. We hope EconCSLib can help fill this gap and make formalization in these areas easier and more reusable. The current version contains foundational material in game theory, social choice, and mechanism design, together with a growing collection of basic results and examples.

EconCSLib is developed with AI in the loop: AI tools have assisted with routine proof engineering, maintenance, and documentation. Humans remain responsible for reviewing definition/theorem statements and public API decisions. The code standards are lighter than Mathlib's, which allows us to iterate quickly while exploring a relatively new formalization domain.

We welcome comments, suggestions, bug reports, and contributions of all kinds. In particular, we would love to hear from both Lean users and researchers working in EconCS and related fields.

Project repository: https://github.com/gametheoryinlean/EconCSLib
